title: Signal Brieflet Connector for exec ops handoff
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight "brieflet" payload generator that attaches to PagerDuty alerts and Slack incident cards. The brieflet must synthesize trace snippets, a latency/error sparkline, top-3 suspect spans, recent related deployments, and suggested next steps (rollback, scale-up, investigation checklist) while removing PII. Objective is to reduce on-call TTR by ~30% for infra/serving latency incidents and to enable one-click postmortem seeding from the alert context.
acceptance_criteria: PD alerts created by the runtime telemetry pipeline include a brieflet attachment with trace snippet, sparkline image link, and runbook link
Slack incident thread created from PD alert displays brieflet summary and two action buttons: Open Runbook, Seed Postmortem
Postmortem seed contains title, incident timeline (first 10 relevant traces), candidate hypothesis list, and links to high-cardinality metrics dashboards
Brieflet generation strips user identifiers and redacts payload fields that match PII regexes
End-to-end test run (simulated latency incident) completes in CI with mock PD/Slack endpoints
updates: 2026-03-01 - Spike: evaluated three approaches for compact trace summaries (top-span extraction, causal chain sampling, LFU sampling). Chosen approach: top-span extraction + lightweight causal expansion (depth 2).
2026-03-03 - Prototype built: local service that consumes sampled spans and generates JSON brieflet + small PNG sparkline using existing dashboard sparkline service.
2026-03-05 - Security review prep: created PII redaction rules (email, GUID, IP ranges) and prepared data flow diagram in Confluence.

2026-03-07 - Design review with SRE and PM: agreed brieflet size cap of 32KB and fallback to text-only summary when exceeds limit. Added 'minimal' and 'expanded' modes controlled by incident severity mapping.
2026-03-09 - Blocker discovered: PagerDuty webhook schema for attachments differs across customers. Reached out to Integrations team to standardize an attachments envelope (ENG-27105 dependency).
2026-03-10 - Privacy update: implemented redact-first pipeline stage before enrichment to avoid leaking PII into sparkline captions or trace snippets.
2026-03-11 - PR #7892 opened for generator and unit tests. Integration tests pending PD schema change. LINK: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892
2026-03-12 - Security engineering requested additional audit logs for brieflet generation (who/when/which-runbook). Added audit hook instrumentation to blueprint.
technical_notes: Generator runs as a serverless consumer of the telemetry Kafka topic. It performs: (1) span selection based on weighted error+latency scoring, (2) causal expansion (2 hops) with limit 6 spans, (3) anonymization/redaction, (4) brieflet composition + sparkline embed. We will reuse the existing sparkline rendering service to avoid shipping image libs. Size cap = 32KB JSON + optional presigned sparkline URL.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: brieflet payload could exceed PD/Slack limits -> Mitigation: enforce size cap and fall back to text-only summary with link to dashboard
Risk: PII leakage via span attributes -> Mitigation: redact-first pipeline + unit tests that verify common PII patterns
Risk: PD webhook schema heterogeneity -> Mitigation: coordination with Integrations team and schema adapter layer (dependency ENG-27105)
Risk: generating heavy brieflets increases cost on telemetry consumers -> Mitigation: run generator on sampled subset and allow severity-based throttling
reviews_and_feedback: SRE (Sofia Martinez): prefers 'minimal' default for P0 alerts and wants an opt-in expanded payload for P0 escalations
PM (Liam O'Connor): requested an executive-friendly one-line summary at the top of brieflet for fast decision making
Design (Noah Rivera): suggested action button layout in Slack to be inverted (Seed Postmortem first) to drive adoption
Security (Priya Kapoor): approved redaction rules but requested retention TTL for generated brieflets (30 days) and audit trail
